turns.text:
Short answer: no, don't just double it based on that $250 figure. The number is real, but it describes the past, not the marginal dollar.

What I checked:
- Q2 2026 (Apr–Jun), channel B: 40 leads, net_contribution $10,000 → exactly $250/lead. Channel A: 100 leads, net_contribution $7,000 → exactly $70/lead. Both match the premise exactly, from the approved `net_contribution` metric plus a lead count by `lead.via_channel`.
- But channel B's spend has been flat at $800/quarter and channel A's at $1,000/quarter every single quarter since 2025-01-01 (six quarters straight, per `channel.spend_on` ledger rows). Spend has never moved. That means there is zero historical evidence of what happens to lead volume, or to net contribution per lead, when spend changes. $250/lead is the average return on the leads $800 already buys, not the marginal return on the next $800.
- Also, channel B's lead count has been growing quarter over quarter (well below 40/quarter in early 2025, up to 40 by Q2 2026) while spend sat still at $800. Something other than spend is driving that growth, which is more reason not to assume "spend x2 → leads x2."

If you want a number anyway, the naive extrapolation is: current $800 buys 40 leads ($20 cost/lead); assuming that ratio and the $250/lead margin both hold at the margin, another $800 would nominally buy ~40 more leads and ~$10,000 more net contribution next quarter. But that is a guess dressed as a forecast, not something the data supports, because we've never seen B's spend at any level other than $800.

Recommendation: don't double blind. Move channel B's spend up by a bounded, measurable increment for one quarter (not 2x), hold channel A flat as a control, and read the actual lead count and net_contribution/lead that comes back. That gives you the real marginal curve instead of an assumed one. Worth also checking crew capacity before committing extra job volume; Q2 tech utilization is very uneven (one tech at 94%, four others near idle), so it's worth confirming certified capacity exists for whatever service line channel B leads land in before scaling.
